A palm-sized fae perched on a jar rim, deep-rose petal-silk bodice bright against terracotta clay, copper hair loose and wild, lacewing-gold wings half-raised, tipping dried seeds one by one into a phial as tall as her forearm.
A wren sitting on the stone windowsill among the jars, whole and puffed and warm-brown, head tipped sideways, one small claw resting on the neck of a green bottle.

A palm-sized fae standing on the counter beside a cluster of corked phials, violet leaf-dress layered and full, dark braided hair wound with a grass twist, beetle-shell-iridescent wings flat and still, hauling a phial twice her height upright in a woven-rush sling.
A fat bumbling moth resting on the counter's edge in a warm glow from the nearest lantern, wings spread and dust-pale, antennae trembling, perfectly whole and calm.

A palm-sized fae tucked into a deep shelf-bay among earthenware pots, sapphire moss-velvet tunic, auburn hair pinned with a bent twig, dragonfly-clear wings folded close, tying a bundle of dried thyme with a thread of spider-silk.
A robin perched on the rim of a wide stoneware pot near the door, round and red-breasted and complete, perfectly still, one black eye watching the room.

A palm-sized fae sitting cross-legged on the loft rail far above the counter, emerald woven-grass wrap belted with twisted root, white hair falling loose to her waist, petal wings iridescent green, sorting small seeds into a row of thimble-sized pots balanced along the rail beside her.
A hedgehog dozing in a patch of soft sun on the lowest shelf, whole and spined and small-snouted, tucked into a half-coil, breathing slowly.

A palm-sized fae perched on a hook hammered into a beam, hanging upside-down to reach a low shelf below, marigold petal-silk bodice pooling at her shoulders, dark skin, black hair swinging free, dragonfly wings spread wide for balance, fingers closing around a small clay pot.
A field mouse sitting on the rim of a stoneware pot near the back wall, whole and bright-eyed and trembling-whiskered, both forepaws pressed together, quite at home.

A palm-sized fae standing halfway up the ladder, one hand gripping a rung, the other pressing a bundle of dried lavender stems to her chest, deep-rose layered skirts snagging gently on the wood, luna-moth-green wings fanned out for balance, silver hair in a long plait over one shoulder.
A red squirrel curled in an empty willow basket on the upper shelf, whole and flame-furred, bushy tail curved over its back, chin resting on its own forepaws.

A palm-sized fae seated on the counter's edge, legs dangling, a glowing amber jar set before her casting soft light upward across her face, warm brown skin, dark curls loose, violet petal-silk dress, using the jar's glow to examine a single dried flower held up between two fingers.
A toad sitting on the flagstone floor beside the counter's foot, whole and broad and mottled gold-brown, unmoving, dignified, perfectly settled as though it has always been there.

A palm-sized fae perched on a shelf among tall corked bottles, emerald woven-grass skirts spread around her, red hair in two short plaits, beetle-shell wings catching the lantern light, filling a small phial from a clay spoon with careful tilted concentration.
A snail moving very slowly along the outer edge of the lowest shelf, whole shell spiralled amber and cream, soft body extended, leaving the faintest damp trail behind it.

A palm-sized fae standing on the counter with both arms raised, balancing a single drop of warm amber light on the tip of one finger, marigold bodice glowing against the dim room, pale gold hair unbound, lacewing-gold wings trembling with the effort of keeping still.
A bumblebee resting on the lip of an open jar, whole and round and furred in gold and black, wings folded, legs dusted with pale powder, quietly at rest.

A palm-sized fae asleep inside a large wooden acorn-measure on the side table, only her face and copper hair and the furled edge of her lacewing wings visible above the rim, a deep-rose wrap tucked around her shoulders.
A wood-mouse on the counter beside a cluster of dried herbs, whole and enormous-eared and honey-furred, sitting up on its haunches, nose working busily at the air.

A palm-sized fae standing on a floating dried seed-head drifting at shelf height in a slow air current, riding it like a raft with both arms slightly out, sapphire leaf-dress brilliant against the shadowed shelves, black hair cut blunt at the jaw, petal wings folded and trusting.
A small tortoise on the flagstone floor near the hearth, whole and domed and slow, head just extended from the shell, blinking in the warmth of the soft glow from the embers.

A palm-sized fae perched on the very top of a tall cabinet, violet petal-silk bodice over a layered birch-bark skirt, dark braided hair with tiny white flowers pressed through it, luna-moth wings spread full and luminous green, tying off a long rope of twisted herb-stems she has been plaiting.
A folded sleeping bat hanging from a ceiling hook in the far corner of the room, whole and small and silk-eared, wings wrapped around itself like a soft cloak, utterly still.

A palm-sized fae kneeling at the edge of the counter, coral-brown skin, loose dark curls falling forward, deep-rose petal-silk dress, dragonfly-clear wings at rest, carefully fitting a tiny stopper of wax into the neck of a phial with both thumbs pressed firm.
